$comment: Demo data (CLAUDE.md 1.2). Twelve original problems for the Phase 3 prototype; hidden tests are not here, only their recorded outcomes in submissions.json.

problems.title: Ledger reconciliation
problems.statementMd:
Your ledger records every payment you expect to clear. The bank sends a statement of what actually cleared. An entry is **confirmed** when the statement holds a line with the same reference and the same amount in cents.

Return the ids of ledger entries the statement does not confirm, in ledger order.

A statement line confirms at most one ledger entry. If the ledger holds the same reference and amount twice, the statement must hold it twice too.
constraints: References are 1 to 16 letters and digits

problems.title: Merge overlapping bookings
problems.statementMd:
A meeting room's bookings arrive as `[start, end]` pairs in minutes since midnight, in no particular order. Two bookings that overlap or touch (one ends the minute the other starts) belong to one block.

Return the blocks, sorted by start.

problems.title: Sliding window maximum
problems.statementMd:
A sensor reports one temperature reading per second. For every window of `k` consecutive readings, report the highest reading in that window.

Return the maxima in window order. When there are fewer than `k` readings, return an empty list.

problems.title: Idempotent payment capture
problems.statementMd:
A payment gateway retries requests when the network drops, so the same capture can arrive more than once. Each request carries an idempotency key, an account and an amount in cents.

Process the requests in order. The first request with a key captures the amount. A later request with the same key and the same account and amount is a retry: it captures nothing and returns the first result. A later request with the same key but a different account or amount is rejected as a conflict.

Return the balance captured per account, and the list of rejected request indexes.
constraints: Balances fit in a 64-bit signed integer

problems.title: Split a bill to the cent
problems.statementMd:
Split a bill of `total` cents between people by weight. Each person's share is their weight's fraction of the total, rounded down to a whole cent. The cents left over go one each to the people with the largest discarded fractions, ties broken by position.

The shares must add up to the total exactly.

problems.title: Token bucket rate limiter
problems.statementMd:
Each client of an API has a bucket that holds at most `capacity` tokens and refills at `rate` tokens per second, continuously. A request costs one token. A bucket starts full.

Given requests as `(timestamp in milliseconds, client)` sorted by time, return for each request whether it is allowed.

problems.title: Slowest endpoints in an access log
problems.statementMd:
Each line of an access log reads `METHOD PATH STATUS MILLISECONDS`. Lines that do not match this shape are skipped.

Return the `k` endpoints (method and path together) with the highest median response time, slowest first. Break ties by endpoint name.

samples.input:
k: 1
GET /a 200 30
GET /a 200 50
POST /b 201 45
broken line

problems.title: Fewest transfers between stations
problems.statementMd:
A rail network has numbered lines; each line is a list of stations it stops at. Riding a line between any two of its stops costs nothing; changing lines costs one transfer.

Return the fewest transfers needed to get from station `from` to station `to`, or `-1` when it cannot be done. Staying on the first line you board costs zero.

problems.title: Fewest coins for change
problems.statementMd: A till holds unlimited coins of each listed value. Return the fewest coins that add up to `amount` exactly, or `-1` when no combination does. An amount of zero needs zero coins.

samples.note: Five plus five plus five; twelve first needs four coins.

problems.title: Two transfers that net to zero
problems.statementMd: An audit flags pairs of transfers that cancel each other out. Given signed amounts in cents, return the indexes `[i, j]` with `i < j` of the first pair, in order of `j`, whose amounts add up to zero. Return an empty list when there is none.

samples.note: A single zero has no partner.

problems.title: Top merchants by volume
problems.statementMd: Card transactions stream in as `(merchant, cents)`. Return the `k` merchants with the highest total volume, highest first, ties broken by merchant name. Refunds arrive as negative amounts and count against the total.

problems.title: The double-entry ledger
problems.statementMd:
Every posting in a double-entry ledger debits one account and credits another by the same amount, under a journal id. A journal is **balanced** when its debits equal its credits.

You receive postings in arrival order, some of them duplicated by a faulty importer and some journals cut short.

1. Drop exact duplicate postings (same journal, accounts, amount and sequence number).
2. Report every journal that is still unbalanced, with the amount it is off by.
3. For the balanced journals, return each account's closing balance.

Report journals in the order their first posting arrived.
constraints: Amounts are whole cents up to 10^12

samples.input: [(j1, cash, sales, 500, 1), (j1, cash, sales, 500, 1), (j2, bank, cash, 200, 1)]
